note.backdrop: A give-back before the open after Monday's surge: S&P 500 -1.1%, Nasdaq 100 -2.0%, VIX +8.1%, semiconductors' median -4.4%. The stories frame it as traders reassessing Monday's Nvidia-led rally and the AI buildout (WSJ, Yahoo). The give-back is uneven: Nvidia has returned about a fifth of Monday's +31.48%, Micron about two-fifths of its +19.04%, HPE nearly four-fifths after its report (StockTitan). Outside chips the morning belongs to company news: Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $175 a share in cash, and seven retailers reported, most of them up. 4 of 2451 stocks are outside their 9-in-10 range: Shoe Station and Insmed on their news; Summit Hotel and Wintrust with none.

read.says: Before the open Nov 24: QQQ -1.74% and SPY -0.90% at 6:34-6:35 a.m. ET; Nvidia -5.34%, Micron -6.94%, Intel -6.62%, HPE -11.64%; Sanofi to buy Insmed for $175 a share in cash (about $41.0 billion, 46% above the Nov 18 close, closing expected in the first half of 2027), Insmed +14.64%, Sanofi +6.46%; Dick's +15.58% and Abercrombie +10.22% on raised outlooks; Burlington +9.50%, Kohl's +8.87%, Dollar Tree +8.20%, Best Buy +5.67%; Shoe Station -23.47%; Semtech -10.60%; Analog Devices -9.44%; Dell, Workday, HP and Autodesk report after the close; GDP and PCE Wednesday 8:30 a.m. ET.

singles.beneath: +14.6%, trading about $4 below $175 before the open: the gap pays for a wait to mid-2027 and the deal's risk (inferred). Its lung drug Brinsupri brought $1.09 billion from its August 2025 launch to Sept 30, 2026. Sanofi, the buyer paying cash, rose 6.5%, unlike CrowdStrike paying in shares on Monday.
singles.cause: Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $175 a share in cash, about $41.0 billion: 46% above its Nov 18 close, before reports of a deal, and about 17.5% above Monday's close. Both boards approved; it needs Insmed's shareholders and regulators, and Sanofi expects to close in the first half of 2027.

themes.mechanism: The read is margins, not demand: AI servers sell more but earn less per dollar, as memory and component costs rise. Dell, HPE's closest partner (0.69) and the next report, is -6.9% before its own results tonight; Super Micro -4.5%.
